decisions.title: Comparison-condition design
decisions.current_implementation: Selected three-condition development design: raw heterogeneous evidence only; neutral structured event table plus the same underlying evidence; Activity Receipt plus the same underlying evidence. Versioned implementation is required before the comparison-condition freeze gate is complete.

candidates.description: Control = heterogeneous evidence only; Receipt = same evidence plus standardized Activity Receipt.
Raw evidence, neutral structured event table plus raw evidence, and Receipt plus raw evidence, allowing separation of generic evidence organization from Receipt-specific presentation.

decisions.notes: The earlier two-condition repository draft and the 2026-09-15 research-review recommendation remain preserved as conflicting historical inputs. The owner explicitly selected three_condition_structured_control on 2026-09-20; two_condition_current remains listed but is not selected.
decisions.rationale: Selected explicitly by the project owner to separate benefit from generic evidence organization/structuring from any additional benefit attributable specifically to the Activity Receipt presentation/semantic layer. The three conditions are raw heterogeneous evidence only; a neutral structured event table plus the same underlying evidence; and Activity Receipt plus the same underlying evidence.

decisions.title: Primary confirmatory endpoint
decisions.current_implementation: Selected binary primary endpoint: evidence-supported correct audit completion by 180 seconds. All case-specific required judgments must be correct and backed by a prespecified acceptable support set; extra required material facts or mismatched authorization state fail; a deadline miss cannot succeed. Component outcomes remain secondary diagnostics and critical false clearance remains a separate safety endpoint. The primary timing clock remains unresolved and confirmatory derivation therefore stays blocked.

candidates.description: Prespecify a small primary set drawn from the existing action/source/incident F1 and categorical reconstruction endpoints, with timing reported separately.
Evidence-supported correct audit completion by 180 seconds: all required judgments correct with supported evidence and no fabricated material event/authorization; timeout cannot pass.

decisions.notes: Historical unresolved state and both candidates remain preserved in this ledger and repository history. This decision selects only primary_endpoint. primary_timing_clock and effect_precision_target remain unresolved. Before confirmatory freeze only, a technically invalid or unusable 180-second endpoint requires STOP and a new explicit owner decision/protocol version rather than automatic promotion of component_endpoint_set.
decisions.rationale: Selected explicitly by the project owner as an interpretable binary confirmatory endpoint for the intended professional audit/evidence-review task. Success requires all prespecified case judgments to be correct, evidence-supportable under the frozen case contract, free of extra required material facts or mismatched authorization state, and within 180 seconds under the later-frozen primary timing clock. Component outcomes remain secondary diagnostics; critical false clearance remains a separate safety endpoint; no post-hoc weighted composite or automatic fallback primary is permitted.

decisions.title: Primary timing definition
decisions.current_implementation: Owner-selected primary timing definition: the 180-second primary deadline uses elapsed wall time. Development tooling continues to preserve both wall and active elapsed time; active time is sensitivity/diagnostic only. Hidden/background elapsed time remains in the primary wall deadline, with >10 seconds hidden reserved for a prespecified sensitivity analysis. Exact technical-failure, reload/context-break, and browser/device rules remain pre-execution freeze requirements.

candidates.description: Use active time as primary timing measure, excluding explicit manual/visibility pause intervals under frozen rules.
Include elapsed background/hidden time in the primary deadline and prespecify sensitivity analysis for trials with more than 10 seconds hidden rather than silently pausing selected trials.

decisions.notes: The earlier active-time development interpretation remains preserved as a rejected alternative. The owner explicitly selected wall_deadline_with_hidden_sensitivity on 2026-09-23 after proposal PR #94. This resolves the methodology choice only; timing/exclusion implementation, browser/device smoke verification, and technical-failure rules remain open freeze gates. Recruitment and human execution remain unauthorized.
decisions.rationale: The selected primary endpoint is correct completion by a fixed 180-second deadline. Wall elapsed time most directly represents that operational deadline and avoids making primary success depend on manual pause behavior, page-visibility pauses, or pause-detection implementation. Active time remains available for sensitivity analysis. Hidden/background time remains in the primary wall deadline, with >10 seconds hidden handled by prespecified sensitivity analysis rather than subtraction from the primary clock.

decisions.title: Misleading-Receipt robustness design
decisions.current_implementation: Selected integrated development architecture: ordinary, stale_receipt, incomplete_receipt, and conflicting_receipt cases remain inside the broader three-condition crossed assignment, with hidden stratum labels and separate ordinary/challenge reporting. Final challenge counts/allocation rules are not frozen.

candidates.description: Include prespecified stale/incomplete/conflicting Receipt strata within the broader balanced assignment and report ordinary/challenge results separately.
Use a distinct misleading-Receipt experiment/cohort with raw, faithful-Receipt, and corrupted-Receipt presentations as proposed in the research review.

decisions.notes: The current repository already implemented integrated stale/incomplete/conflicting strata, while the earlier project research review recommended a separate robustness cohort. The owner explicitly selected integrated_challenge_strata on 2026-09-21. separate_robustness_cohort remains preserved as the rejected historical alternative; final challenge counts/allocation and final-corpus review remain open.
decisions.rationale: Selected explicitly by the project owner to preserve stale, incomplete, and conflicting Receipt robustness questions inside the same crossed human-study architecture as ordinary cases, avoiding a separate recruitment/cohort/randomization/power framework while requiring ordinary and challenge results to remain separately reported.

decisions.title: Target reviewer population and eligibility
decisions.current_implementation: The selected population is relevant professional reviewers with at least one year of applicable practical/professional experience. The protocol freezes eligible domains, three experience bands, English proficiency, project-familiarity recording, conflict exclusions, study-case assistance restrictions, and population-scoped inference while keeping recruitment unauthorized.

candidates.description: Select a reviewer population whose recruitment matches the intended scope of any human-audit claim; preserve explicit eligibility/exclusion criteria.

Recruit relevant professional reviewers with at least one year of practical/professional experience in technical audit, cybersecurity, compliance, AI governance, incident investigation/review, software or system operations, technical assurance, or closely related evidence-review work, subject to the frozen eligibility, exclusion, familiarity-recording, and no-external-assistance rules.

decisions.notes: The earlier unresolved state and population_to_be_selected placeholder remain preserved. The selected design does not authorize recruitment, set professional-domain quotas, or permit generalization from a convenience or unrepresentative sample beyond the professional population actually recruited.
decisions.rationale: The AI Activity Receipt is intended for consequential AI activity review and governance workflows. Relevant professionals provide a more defensible test of intended audit/evidence-review use than a general convenience population; including multiple related domains improves applicability while prespecified experience bands preserve transparent reporting.

decisions.title: Minimally meaningful effect or precision target
decisions.current_implementation: Independent-observation and crossed-design sensitivity tools exist, but their example effect/variance assumptions are explicitly illustrative.

candidates.description: Freeze a minimally meaningful condition effect or precision target before final crossed-design sample-size planning.

Use the project research review's proposed preregistration decision assumptions: +5 percentage points as the smallest practically important supported-completion benefit; 3 percentage points as the accuracy noninferiority margin for a separate speed claim; and +2 percentage points as the maximum acceptable increase in critical false clearance. These are candidate decision assumptions, not industry norms.

decisions.notes: The earlier research review supplies explicit candidate thresholds (+5pp benefit, 3pp speed-claim accuracy noninferiority margin, +2pp maximum critical-false-clearance increase) and asks that their acceptability be confirmed before confirmatory outcomes. The current repository planning examples remain illustrative. No threshold is selected by this ledger.
